\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Normalized Blocks}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.NormalizedBlocks
\section{Overview}
Convergence against scalar Lipschitz tests passes to bounded continuous tests of finite products of probability laws. In particular, independent normalized Boolean blocks converge to a standard Gaussian vector.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Finite products from scalar Lipschitz convergence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_pi_of_scalar_lipschitz}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\mu_m$ and $\nu$ be probability measures on $\mathbb R$. Assume that for every $c\ge0$ and every $c$-Lipschitz $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $\int\psi\,d\mu_m\to\int\psi\,d\nu$. Then for each $n\ge0$ and every bounded continuous $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, $\int F\,d\mu_m^{\otimes n}\to\int F\,d\nu^{\otimes n}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Normalized Boolean sum law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolSumLaw}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
For $m\ge0$, let $\nu_m$ be the probability law of $(m+1)^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{m+1}\epsilon_j$, where the $\epsilon_j$ are independent uniform signs in $\{-1,1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian limit for products of sum laws]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_normalizedBoolSum_pi}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolSumLaw,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_normalizedBoolSum,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_pi_of_scalar_lipschitz,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure,BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Let $\nu_m$ be the law of the normalized sum of $m+1$ independent uniform signs. For every $n\ge0$ and bounded continuous $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, $\int F\,d\nu_m^{\otimes n}\to\int F\,d\gamma_n$ as $m\to\infty$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian limit for independent Boolean blocks]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_normalizedBoolBlocks}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolSumLaw,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_normalizedBoolSum_pi,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure,BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For independent uniform bits $X_{ij}$, put $S_r(X)_i=r^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^r(-1)^{X_{ij}}$. For every $n\ge0$ and bounded continuous $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, $\mathbb E F(S_{m+1}(X))\to\int F\,d\gamma_n$ as $m\to\infty$.
\end{lemma}
